'''''Calla''''' is a genus of [[flowering plant]] in the family [[Araceae]], containing the single species '''''Calla palustris''''' ('''bog arum''', '''marsh calla''', '''wild calla''', '''squaw claw''', and '''water-arum'''<ref name=ROM>Dickinson, T.; Metsger, D.; Bull, J.; & Dickinson, R. (2004) ROM Field Guide to Wildflowers of Ontario. Toronto:Royal Ontario Museum, p. 62.</ref>). It is the only genus in the tribe '''Calleae''' of the subfamily [[Aroideae]]. Its systematic position has been described as "puzzling",<ref name=UlriHessBrödBogn13/> and it has also been placed in its own family '''Callaceae''' and its own subfamily '''Calloideae'''.

== Description ==
It is a [[rhizome|rhizomatous]] [[herbaceous]] [[perennial plant]] growing in [[bog]]s and [[pond]]s. The [[leaves]] are rounded to heart-shaped, {{cvt|6|–|12|cm|frac=4}} long on a {{cvt|10|–|20|cm|0}} [[Petiole (botany)|petiole]], and {{cvt|4|–|12|cm|frac=4}} broad. The greenish-yellow [[inflorescence]] is produced on a [[spadix (botany)|spadix]] about {{cvt|4|–|6|cm|frac=4}} long, enclosed in a white [[spathe]]. The [[fruit]] is a cluster of red [[berry (botany)|berries]], each berry containing several [[seed]]s.<ref>{{eFloras|1|0027260|Calla palustris |first=Sue A. |last=Thompson |family=Araceae}}</ref><ref>{{eFloras|2|200027260|Calla palustris |first1=Heng |last1=Li |first2=Peter C. |last2=Boyce |first3=Josef |last3=Bogner |family=Araceae}}</ref>

The plant is very [[poison]]ous when fresh due to its high [[oxalic acid]] content, but the [[rhizome]] (like that of ''[[Caladium]]'', ''[[Colocasia]]'', and ''[[Arum]]'') is edible after drying, grinding, leaching and boiling.<ref>{{PFAF|Calla palustris}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.epharmacognosy.com/2012/05/wild-calla-calla-palustris-poisonous.html |website=Pharmacognosy |title=Wild calla-Calla palustris-Poisonous plants}}</ref>

== Taxonomy ==
The genus ''Calla'' and its sole species ''Calla palustris'' were first described by [[Carl Linnaeus]] in 1753.<ref name=POWO_2733-1>{{Cite POWO|title=''Calla'' L..|id=2733-1|access-date=2026-01-10|mode=cs1}}</ref> The genus formerly also included a number of other species, which have now been transferred to the separate genus ''[[Zantedeschia]]''. These plants from tropical Africa, however, are still often termed "calla lilies" but should not be confused with ''C. palustris''.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-04-03 |title=Calla Lily Care: Grow Stunning Blooms All Season Long |url=https://www.plantgardener.com/caring-for-calla-lilies/ |access-date=2024-06-03 |website=www.plantgardener.com |language=en-us}}</ref>

The genus ''Calla'' has been regarded as a "puzzling case" in relation to its systematic position. Its pollen is unusual within the family Araceae. The pollen grains are small, ornamented differently, and with a differently constructed [[Pollen#Structure|exine]]. Treatments based on anatomy and morphology have tended to separate ''Calla'' from other aroids.<ref name=UlriHessBrödBogn13/> It has been placed in its own family, Callaceae,<ref name="APweb"/> or in its own subfamily Calloideae within the Araceae.<ref name=UlriHessBrödBogn13/> (In the [[Engler system]], Calloideae had included the genera now placed in [[Orontioideae]].<ref name=MayoBognCusi13>{{Citation |last1=Mayo |first1=Simon J. |last2=Bogner |first2=Josef |last3=Cusimano |first3=Natalie |date=2013 |editor1-last=Wilkin and |editor1-first=P. |editor2-last=Mayo |editor2-first=S. J. |contribution=Recent progress in the phylogenetics and classification of Araceae |title=Early Events in Monocot Evolution |pages=208–242 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |contribution-url=https://cate-araceae.myspecies.info/sites/araceae.e-monocot.org/files/Mayo%20et%20al%202013%20Recent%20progress%20in%20phylogenetics%20Araceae.pdf |access-date=2026-01-10 |name-list-style=amp |mode=cs1}}</ref>) [[Molecular phylogenetics|Molecular phylogenetic]] studies on the other hand place ''Calla'' within the subfamily Aroideae,<ref name=UlriHessBrödBogn13>{{Cite journal |last1=Ulrich |first1=Silvia |last2=Hesse |first2=Michael |last3=Bröderbauer |first3=David |last4=Bogner |first4=Josef |last5=Weber |first5=Martina |last6=Halbritter |first6=Heidemarie |date=2013 |title=''Calla palustris'' (Araceae): New palynological insights with special regard to its controversial systematic position and to closely related genera |journal=Taxon |volume=62 |issue=4 |pages=701–712 |doi=10.12705/624.34 |pmc=4374111 |name-list-style=amp }}</ref> where it may be given its own tribe Calleae.<ref name="APweb">Stevens, P.F. (2001 onwards). [https://www.mobot.org/mobot/research/apweb/orders/alismatalesweb.htm#Calleae "Calleae"]. ''Angiosperm Phylogeny Website''. Retrieved 2026-01-10.</ref>

== Distribution ==
It is native to cool temperate regions of the [[Northern Hemisphere]], in central, eastern and northern Europe (France and Norway eastward, but not Britain), northern Asia and northern North America ([[Alaska]], Canada, and northeastern contiguous United States).<ref name=POWO_2733-1/><ref>Govaerts, R. & Frodin, D.G. (2002). World Checklist and Bibliography of Araceae (and Acoraceae): 1–560. The Board of Trustees of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew.</ref>
